findings.claim: Core Keycloak does not enforce single use for recovery codes stored through the generic user-storage path. It leaves consuming a used code entirely to the user-storage provider, with no guidance.

RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator takes the credential returned by getCredential(), which may come from user storage, makes the allCodesUsed decision on it, and calls removeStoredCredentialById(). That method only removes local/fed-storage credentials, so the provider's copy is not removed. When local and federated credentials both exist, the authenticator inspects or removes a different credential from the one that validated.

When createRecoveryCodesCredential stores codes in user storage (updateCredential returns true), it returns without calling recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(), so existing local recovery-code credentials are not deleted and old codes remain valid.

The test calls TestAppHelper.logout(), which relies on a refreshToken set by completeLogin(), but never calls completeLogin() after submitting the recovery code, so logout may be a no-op and leave sessions behind.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
